first_impression.reaction: Googled 'honeymoon planner cost' because I want a number to drop into my comparison spreadsheet. The intro tells me straight up I won't get one: 'A number on its own tells you very little.' My first thought was 'that's a dodge'. Then I went to the FAQ and the questions list, and they're actually what I'd ask: flat fee, percentage, supplier commissions, get it in writing. A planner's own blog telling me to ask about commissions is more than most do. It's sourced, dated, no 'award-winning' fluff. My problem is the Wedded Wonderland section: it says the questions 'already have answers' but only tells me the fee is agreed in writing, not how it's worked out or whether they take a cut.

journey.quote: A number on its own tells you very little.
journey.reaction: Maybe true, but it's also what every business says when it doesn't want to give a number. I searched 'cost'. I'll read on, but this is on notice.

journey.quote: It closes with how the fee is set when you plan with Wedded Wonderland.
journey.reaction: Good, that's the bit I want. Holding them to it.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: The trip itself (flights, stays, dinners, a boat for a day) is paid to the suppliers who provide it.
journey.reaction: Splitting the fee from the trip is the right way to think about it. That's how I'd set up the spreadsheet anyway.

journey.section: What you are paying a planner for
journey.quote: You give nothing up by handing the trip to someone else.
journey.reaction: And they don't claim you gain anything either. Honest, and backed by the consumer guarantees point.

journey.quote: A planner sets their own fee, so the only reliable figure is the one they put in writing for you.
journey.reaction: Fair. Not what I wanted, but I can't argue with it.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: Do you receive commissions from the suppliers you book, and will you tell us which?
journey.reaction: That's my question, word for word near enough. Credit to them for putting it on their own page.

journey.section: How planners may charge, as questions to ask
journey.quote: Is any part of your fee a percentage of the cost of the trip?
journey.reaction: Good, but the list stops at commissions. A planner can honestly say 'no commission' and still add a mark-up to the supplier price. There's no question about mark-ups or seeing the supplier's own price.

journey.quote: Travel provider or agent insolvency is commonly left out of cancellation cover, and only some agents hold insolvency insurance, so ask your planner directly.
journey.reaction: Useful and protective. After my last vendor, this is exactly the kind of thing I check.

journey.quote: Some banks allow a chargeback, reversing a disputed card transaction, if you do not receive what you paid for, and you should not accept contract terms that ask you to give up chargeback rights.
journey.reaction: A planner telling me how to protect myself from planners. Dated 'As at November 2026' and linked to government sources. Good.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: Meet your Wedded Advisor, and agree the fee.
journey.reaction: The heading says 'How the fee works' and the intro promised 'how the fee is set'. What I get is: it's agreed in writing. That's when, not how. Flat? Percentage? Commission? Nothing.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.
journey.reaction: Not all of them. The commission question is above and this section doesn't answer it. Reads like a claim to have ticked my checklist when they've ticked half of it. This is the one line that cost them trust.

journey.section: How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland
journey.quote: We plan travel anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Big claim, nothing behind it. I'd check it.

journey.quote: Each planner sets their own fee, and it depends on how they charge and on the trip you want.
journey.reaction: Read this first. No figure, no range. Consistent with the rest of the page at least, and the follow-up questions are useful.

journey.quote: Ask for the planner's fee and the cost of flights, stays and experiences to be shown separately, so you can see each one clearly.
journey.reaction: Practical. Going straight into the spreadsheet.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Wonderland fee worked out: flat, percentage of the trip, per booking or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland receive commissions or add mark-ups on the suppliers its Advisor books, and will it disclose which? (deferred business detail)
Even a rough range: what have couples actually paid in planning fees with you? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real honeymoon you've planned, with the fee and the trip cost shown separately. (deferred business detail)
Do you hold insolvency insurance? The page tells me to ask, so I'm asking. (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks or extras through you that I couldn't get booking direct, and are they itemised? (deferred business detail)
When a supplier is paid in another currency, what exchange rate is your AUD quote built on?

turn_offs_found.quote: So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.
turn_offs_found.why: Overclaims. The checklist above includes commissions and how the fee is charged, and this section answers neither. It's exactly the 'marketing hiding the catch' move I look for.

turn_offs_found.quote: It closes with how the fee is set when you plan with Wedded Wonderland.
turn_offs_found.why: Promise not kept. The closing section says when the fee is agreed, not how it is set. Feels like a bait for people like me who skip to the end.

turn_offs_found.quote: We plan travel anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported sweeping claim on a page that otherwise sources everything. Mild, but I notice it.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the 'How planners may charge, as questions to ask' list, as the columns for our three-planner comparison
Our Reddit thread, the 'Protecting what you pay' section, for the insolvency and chargeback points

cta_reaction.quote: Tell your Wedded Advisor the shape of the trip, agree the fee in writing before any work begins, and see every inclusion on paper before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after real evidence, which I respect, and fee-in-writing is the right promise. But I came for cost and the page won't tell me how their fee is worked out or whether they take a cut. They'd go in the spreadsheet and get an email with the six questions, not a booked call.

top_3_changes: Reword 'So the questions above already have answers before you pay: what the fee is, what it covers and what each booking includes, all on paper.' so it doesn't imply every question above is answered, e.g. say your Advisor puts the fee, scope and inclusions on paper before you pay, and invite readers to ask the commission question too. No new business fact needed.

Make the intro promise and heading match what the section delivers: change 'It closes with how the fee is set when you plan with Wedded Wonderland.' and the heading 'How the fee works with Wedded Wonderland' to something like 'how the fee is agreed', since the section covers when and in what form, not the basis.

Add a generic mark-up question to the list after 'Do you receive commissions from the suppliers you book, and will you tell us which?', e.g. ask whether any supplier price includes a mark-up and whether you can see the supplier's own price. Reader advice, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and pricing-type sections first, looked for the catch, flagged overclaims and unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, insolvency cover and perks placed in unanswered_questions as deferred, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Absence of figures not treated as a must-fix; top changes require no new business facts

open_questions.question: Is there a source in the pack that supports a generic 'ask about mark-ups and the supplier's own price' item, alongside the existing commission question?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'honeymoon planner cost' while comparing three planners; relevance is 4 (on topic, but no figures) and enquiry likelihood is 2.
No figures is a deliberate editorial choice; it is voiced as a reaction but not penalised as a must-fix.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, the questions-to-ask list, the protecting-what-you-pay section and the Wedded Wonderland section, with a skim of the rest.
